doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Photographs and the copper printing cut of George Sr.
summary: They talk about when the portrait with his cornet was taken and who holds the copper cut made for a newspaper; his mother said he would rather play than eat.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: I was wondering about the... Well, thank God as well as it is. I was wondering about those pictures that you showed us about when they were taken. If you remember this picture where he's holding his coronet, would you know about when that would be taken? Would that be when he was first married or later on? Oh, no.

Uh-uh. Is that in the... He had this taken. I don't know about that. Well, I'm trying to think who I could make these pictures. You know who had these pictures made? Earl. Earl Joseph. You know he's going to see Naomi? Yeah. Would you want...
I thought you had it. Y'all took the block away from me. That takes everything... You don't tell me it's lost.

You know that block. The block is this is the other part. He had this made to put in a paper. Yes. And I'm trying to think. And the boy that took this cut, he worked in the perfect place. And he made just a bunch of them. And he gave me the other cut. She took that cut away from me. She grabbed everything. She managed to do that. I don't think she threw it away. But you said you made several copies of the film. Oh, yeah. Several copies. I got one or two back there. I know you. She gave me that.

She gave me that. We have this couple of weeks. We want to pay you something for Arthur, too. Yeah, you can't have that room because I got some information. We appreciate it. It's a wonderful picture to have. That's it.
That is him. That is him. Yeah. Yeah. That is him. Well, I tell you.

I never heard. And I don't even. But it was up in years. If he was as good as his son, he was a hound. Even if I'm done. If he was good. If he was better than little George, he must have been a genius. He must have been a genius. What do you call him?
Batman. Him and his music. His mother said. She said, George, you'd rather play music than to eat. He said, Ma, I would.
